%1$s: %2$s

Log in separately in each space and set an app per slot from the hub. Installed apps and optional notification-profile bindings are unrelated to these web sessions.

If the service asks for a secure-storage PIN or blocks WebView, follow its official recovery flow; this app cannot bypass it. Popups, external links, downloads, calls and background push are not supported. Desktop/mobile mode changes only this account. The mobile site is the default because it is the layout that fits every screen size; a service whose phone layout has no messages page at all (TikTok, Zalo, WhatsApp Web) starts on the desktop site instead so its chat list is reachable, and your own switch here always wins from then on. If a dialog still hides its own close button, choose Fit the page to this screen in these options. The floating bubble opens this account screen; the webpage is not drawn inside the overlay.

While this page is on screen, Bop reads nothing from it but its own tab title: an unread marker there updates the card and the bubble badge of this slot as soon as a message arrives, without reading or storing any message text. Leaving the space stops that reading — a hidden page does not poll for hours — and coming back reads the marker again, so a message that arrived in the meantime is still reported. Nothing arrives while the session is closed, so a closed web session still cannot raise an account-has-a-message card.
